newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN STRIKE EARLY IN OPENING TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN STRIKE EARLY IN OPENING TEST.

text.p: New Zealand struggled to 67 for three at lunch on the opening day of the first test against Pakistan on Thursday.
They lost openers Bryan Young and Justin Vaughan for only 16 runs before Adam Parore and Stephen Fleming added 51 for the third wicket..
Vaughan was trapped leg before by paceman Shahid Nazir for three in his sixth over and the in-form Young went in a similar way to Waqar Younis for eight after Lee Germon had won the toss and batted.
Pakistan claimed their third wicket on the stroke of lunch when off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq had Parore smartly caught by Salim Malik for 37.
Parore had struck five fours in 67 balls and seemed set for a big innings when he pushed forward and edged the ball to Malik in the slips.

Pakistan captain Wasim Akram pulled out out of the test at the last minute after complaining of a shoulder pain, raising fears he may miss the entire series against New Zealand. Saeed Anwar led the side.
A similar problem had forced Akram to miss the crucial World Cup semifinal against India and he also skipped one of the matches in the recent Singer Cup at Sharjah..
"I bowled a few overs this morning in the nets to test the shoulder but it remained sore," Akram said.
Akram was replaced by debutant Mohammad Wasim, a middle-order batsman. Opener Zahoor Elahi also gained his first call-up.
New Zealand: B.Young, J.Vaughan, A.Parore, S.Fleming, N.Astle, M.Greatbatch, C.Cairns, C.Harris, L.Germon (captain), D.Patel, S.Doull.
Pakistan: Saeed Anwar (captain), Zahoor Elahi, Ijaz Ahmad, Salim Malik, Inzamamul Haq, Mohammad Wasim, Moin Khan, Saqlain Mushtaq, Mushtaq Ahmad, Waqar Younis, Shahid Nazir.
